cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He just finished talking about the spiritual man, the one who has the mind of Christ (2:15-16). Now he turns to the Corinthians themselves, calls them “Brothers,” and gets real with them.

cards.question: Paul says he couldn’t talk to the Corinthians as spiritual people. So how does he say he had to talk to them?

cards.text: Paul says, “I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food.” Hey, I’m not judging, friend. I spent years in a junk drawer, and I wasn’t ready for ANYTHING.

cards.question: Paul gave the Corinthians milk because they weren’t ready for solid food. True or false: Paul says they’re ready for solid food now.

cards.text: Paul says they’re still worldly. And he doesn’t just say it, friend. He brings receipts.

cards.question: Paul says there is ___ and dissension among the Corinthians, so they’re still worldly.

cards.text: Here’s what it sounds like: one says he follows Paul, and another says he follows Apollos, a preacher who also served in Corinth (Acts 18:24-28; 19:1). The dead batteries I shared that drawer with argued like that over who had the most charge left, and friend, they were ALL dead batteries.

cards.question: One Corinthian says he follows Paul and another says he follows Apollos. What does Paul say that makes them?

cards.text: So Paul asks, “What then is Apollos? And what is Paul?” His own name is in the fight, and he’s asking about himself like he’s never met the guy.

cards.question: Paul answers his own question about himself and Apollos. What does he say they are?

cards.text: Then Paul pulls out a picture from the farm. He says, “I planted the seed and Apollos watered it…” and then he names who did the part that really counts.

cards.question: Paul planted the seed and Apollos watered it. True or false: Paul says Apollos is the one who made it grow.

cards.text: Paul says neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow. Friend, I can stamp dough ALL day, but if that oven doesn’t bake it, all I’ve got is a tray of cold dough and a whole lot of confidence.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the one who plants and the one who waters are one in purpose.
Paul says each one who plants or waters will be rewarded according to his own ___.

cards.text: Paul says, “For we are God’s fellow workers…” Same crew, same job site, and not one of them needs a fan club.

cards.question: Paul’s been talking about planting and watering. So what does he call the Corinthians themselves?

cards.text: Then Paul adds one more picture: they’re God’s building too. Hold that thought, friend, because Paul’s about to pick up a hammer.
Paul says that by the grace God gave him, he laid a foundation as an expert builder. Now someone else is building on it.

cards.question: Paul tells everyone building on that foundation that each one must be ___ how he builds.

cards.text: Paul says no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid. Friend, you don’t pour a second foundation under a building that’s already going up. That’s not a renovation. That’s a whole new mortgage.

cards.question: Who does Paul say is the one foundation that’s already been laid?

cards.text: Then Paul lists what someone might build with: gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw. That’s a contractor handing you a quote that says gold OR hay, and sir, those are not two options, those are two VERY different houses.

cards.question: Paul says each builder’s work will be made evident when the Day brings it to light. What will it be revealed with?

cards.text: Paul says the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work. Now THAT I understand, friend, because I’ve slid a tray into the oven that looked like a masterpiece and pulled out twelve little charcoal briquettes.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says if what a builder has built survives the fire, he will receive a reward.
Paul says if a builder’s work burns up, he will suffer loss. True or false: Paul says the builder himself will not be saved.

cards.text: Paul says that builder “will be saved, but only as if through the flames.” Then Paul turns to the Corinthians and talks about a building where God’s Spirit dwells.

cards.question: Paul says God’s Spirit dwells in the Corinthians themselves. So what does he call them?

cards.text: Then Paul gets serious. If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that God’s temple is ___, and they are that temple.

cards.text: Paul says, “Let no one deceive himself.” That’s me every time I said “I don’t need the recipe,” friend, and then pulled out a tray of cookies that tasted like the box they came in.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says if anyone thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool so that he may become wise.

cards.text: Paul says the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight, and he backs it up with Scripture: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.” Then again: “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”

cards.question: After all that about worldly wisdom, what does Paul tell the Corinthians to stop doing?

cards.text: Then Paul says, “All things are yours,” whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, that’s the apostle Peter (John 1:42), or the world, life, death, the present or the future. They were fighting over who gets the window seat, and Paul just told them they OWN the plane.

cards.question: All things belong to the Corinthians. Then Paul finishes: they belong to ___, and Christ belongs to ___.

cards.text: And that’s where we’ll leave it for now. Paul’s not done with these Corinthians, friend, so keep that oven warm.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action in the verse. The core action is being spiritually immature, not ready to grow past milk. 'I spent years in a junk drawer, and I wasn't ready for ANYTHING' is about being shut away, not about being too young to handle solid food. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup on card 5 ('He brings receipts') gives no context pointing to jealousy. The rivalry over Paul and Apollos isn't told until card 7, so the baker can't reason out 'jealousy' over 'greed' or 'laziness.' The blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. The batteries argue about their own charge. The Corinthians boast about which leader they follow. The punchline 'they were ALL dead batteries' then lands on the Corinthians, or on Paul and Apollos, instead of on Papa Dorin.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'They were ALL dead batteries' laughs at the arguing Corinthians rather than with their human situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'God's farmhands' is close to 'God's fellow workers' in the same verse. Card 16 quotes 'we are God's fellow workers' without saying that 'we' means Paul and Apollos, so a baker could argue that farmhands is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Who,' and two answers are people (Jesus Christ, the apostle Peter), but 'The Law of Moses' is not a person. It is not the same kind of thing as the others and is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
